## Sampling design

See `notebooks/09_sampling_campaign_design.qmd` for the full, reproducible
analysis behind the SBRR/SBGG calibration campaign design; condensed here:

::: {.callout-note}
A two-tier design is recommended: a short (2-4 week), daily-to-sub-daily
intensive chloride-sampling window at both SBRR and SBGG early in the
field season (to establish a real Cl-EC calibration relationship for the
first time), followed by a lower-frequency (biweekly-to-monthly) campaign
for the remainder of the year, with extra samples deliberately bracketing
large storms/spring runoff. A real Monte Carlo subsampling analysis on
the existing conductivity record shows daily sampling keeps reconstruction
error under ~5% of the mean specific conductance at both sites, growing
smoothly (not sharply) as the interval lengthens -- see the notebook for
the full error-vs-interval curve and its caveats.
:::

## PHREEQC modeling methods

See Chapter 2 for the full background on charge balance, saturation
index, the five thermodynamic databases used and why, and the two
geothermometry approaches. Real speciation/saturation-index results exist
for 233 eligible real samples; a real two-end-member mixing run and one
real (partially-parsed, see Chapter 2's caveat) inverse-modeling run have
also been completed.
